newsitem.title: FRANCE: Harvest pressure mounts on French wheat prices.
newsitem.headline: Harvest pressure mounts on French wheat prices.

text.p: Prospects of a bumper harvest in France continue to put pressure on domestic wheat prices, dealers said on Friday.
Wheat into Rouen for September and October-December delivery was down five francs to 875 francs a tonne.
French farmers expect the wheat harvest to jump by some 4.2 million tonnes to a record 34 million, while national grain office ONIC is eyeing 33.8 million tonnes.
Results of a Tunisian tender added to perceptions that prices were on a bearish trend. "This last deal suggests the market anticipates further price falls," one exporter said.
Tunisia bought 175,000 tonnes of soft wheat at $179.87 and $176.87 per tonne, including cost, freight and insurance, for October, November and December shipment.
Dealers described these prices as very low.
